reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Since August 2026, billing dispute tickets have roughly doubled (E-07), driven by a billing-side defect in the billing import/validation step that produces incorrect bills predominantly from ACTUAL (non-estimated) meter reads rather than from estimate substitution (E-01: 59% ACTUAL vs 41% ESTIMATED among disputed bills), with tariff/rate changes ruled out as the mechanism (E-02, E-04).
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Since August 2026, the ESTIMATED-read subset of billing disputes (1240/3025 disputed bills, E-01) has been driven by billing import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-12), which rejects valid, timely AMI reads as high-consumption for 95.5% of these disputes (1184/1240, firmware v4.2, E-11) because it compares raw register values (unit_scaling=none) against 12-month m3 history while firmware v4.2 meters (rollout 2026-06) report readings in '0.1 m3' units (E-13), forcing estimate substitution and triggering disputes in step with the Aug-Sep surge (E-07). The mechanism behind the remaining ACTUAL-read disputed cohort (59%, 1785/3025, E-01) is not yet established and is tracked separately as an open unknown, not adopted as part of this premise.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
